reasoning: The nth derivative of tangent is a polynomial in tan x of degree n+1: differentiation replaces P(t) by (1+t²)P′(t), increasing the degree by one. These functions are distinct, so A is infinite. The derivatives of sin(3x) have amplitudes 3ⁿ; in particular, every fourth derivative is 3^(4k)sin(3x), giving infinitely many distinct functions in B. The derivatives of 3sin x cycle through exactly 3sin x, 3cos x, −3sin x, and −3cos x, so C is finite. Thus A and B only are infinite, agreeing with Math Academy's stated answer.
